studies.title: Hepatic mTORC2 activates glycolysis and lipogenesis through Akt, glucokinase, and SREBP1c
studies.finding: The authors deleted rictor, an essential mTORC2 component, only in mouse liver. In fed knockout mice the liver lost Akt Ser473 phosphorylation and had lower glucokinase and SREBP1c activity, so it kept making glucose (gluconeogenesis) while glycolysis and fat synthesis fell, as if it could not sense that the animal had eaten. studies.title: Adipose-specific knockout of raptor results in lean mice with enhanced mitochondrial respiration
studies.finding: Adipose raptor knockout yields lean, metabolically protected mice, revealing mTORC1's role in fat metabolism.

studies.title: Mammalian TOR complex 2 controls the actin cytoskeleton and is rapamycin insensitive
studies.finding: mTORC2 (rictor) controls the actin cytoskeleton and is rapamycin-insensitive, defining a second mTOR complex in mammals.
